baer-heitev/1:_: Open to one another. See Magen Avraham and Mishna Berurah.
baer-heitev/3:_: The inner one — for it faces the outer one alone, and even though the outer one's eruv was placed in the inner one, it says to it: I sent you for my benefit, not to harm me.
beer-hagolah/1:א: (א) Mishnah Eruvin chapter 5, and Rabbi Shimon.
beer-hagolah/1:ד: (ד) Similar to the middle one — as if dwelling in them and outer residents do not dwell in the middle.
beer-hagolah/1:ו: (ו) For the three are not connected outer to outer.
beer-hagolah/2:א: (א) Mishnah there 45 and in the Gemara.
beer-hagolah/2:ב: (ב) Forbidden foot in its place forbids outside its place.
beer-hagolah/3:ב: (ב) Since its eruv is with it, it can withdraw from the outer one — "for my benefit you opened, not to harm me" — and closes the door and uses for itself.
beer-hagolah/5:_: (ה) In the Gemara there, and Shmuel, Rif, Rosh, and Rambam chapter 4 of laws of Eruvin.
beur-hagra/4:_: (ד) Seif 4. Many like one individual. 73a — father and son, etc., and see Rashi there.
eliyah-rabbah/1:_: (a) Open to one another, etc. — see Mishna Berurah.
kaf-hachayyim/3:_: (3) Eruv in this and that, etc.
mechaber/1:main: The law of courtyards open to one another. And in it are 5 seifim: Three courtyards open to one another and open to reshus ha-rabbim, and each of the outer ones joined with the middle one and the outer ones did not join together — the outer ones are forbidden with one another and the middle one is permitted with each of them and they are permitted with it. When does this apply? When the middle one placed its eruv in this one and its eruv in that one, or the outer ones placed their eruv in the middle one in two houses; but if the two outer ones placed their eruv in the middle one in one house — all three are permitted with one another.
mechaber/2:main: Two courtyards, one within the other, and the inner one open to the outer one and the outer one to an alley, and the inner one has foot-traffic on the outer one — if the inner joined for itself and not the outer, or each joined for itself and one of the outer forgot and did not join — the inner is permitted and the outer forbidden; if the outer joined and not the inner, or each joined for itself and one of the inner forgot and did not join — both are forbidden; if each joined for itself, each is permitted in its courtyard.
mechaber/3:main: They joined together and placed their eruv in the outer one and one — whether of the inner or outer — forgot and did not join — both are forbidden until he nullifies his domain; if they placed their eruv in the inner one and one of the inner forgot and did not join — both are forbidden; but if one of the outer forgot and did not join — the inner is permitted.
mechaber/4:main: If one individual dwells in the inner and one in the outer, or two in the outer and they joined — the individual in the inner does not forbid the outer. {Rama: And likewise many who are like one individual need not join as explained above siman 370 (Maggid chapter 4).}
mechaber/5:main: Three courtyards one within another and one individual in each — even though many tread in the outer one they do not forbid, for each is permitted in its place; if there were two in the inner and did not join, they forbid the individuals in the middle and outer. This is the rule: forbidden foot in its place forbids outside its place; permitted foot in its place does not forbid outside its place.
mishnah-berurah/1:א: (א) Open to one another — otherwise they could not join together.
mishnah-berurah/1:ב: (ב) And open to reshus ha-rabbim — and likewise open to an alley. Later authorities wrote: likewise if only the outer is open to reshus ha-rabbim or alley and the middle has foot-traffic with the inner second one before it — the law is the same: each is permitted with the middle even if the outer is open to reshus ha-rabbim and the inner cannot forbid it — permitted foot in its place does not forbid outside its place, as below seif 2.
mishnah-berurah/1:ג: (ג) Its eruv in this and its eruv in that — then middle residents dwell in the outer and outer residents do not dwell in the middle — all are as one; but if they placed eruv in the middle, it is as if all dwell in the middle.
mishnah-berurah/1:ד: (ד) In two houses — even filling one vessel and leaving remainder and giving afterward to another vessel — in such a case it would help if placed in one house as siman 366 seif 4; but in two houses the outers are not connected to each other.
mishnah-berurah/1:ה: (ה) In one house — one vessel or filled one jug and remainder [later authorities].
mishnah-berurah/1:ו: (ו) All three permitted — as if they joined together.
mishnah-berurah/2:א: (ז) And inner open, etc. — and in each there are residents forbidding one another.
mishnah-berurah/2:ב: (ח) For itself — with residents within it.
mishnah-berurah/2:ג: (ט) Inner permitted — it can close its opening and outer residents cannot prevent it.
mishnah-berurah/2:ד: (י) Outer forbidden — one who did not give share in eruv forbids the rest unless he nullifies his share to them.
mishnah-berurah/2:ה: (יא) Both forbidden — we hold forbidden foot in its place forbids outside its place when there is foot-traffic there unless he nullifies to inner residents and also foot-traffic domain in outer to outer residents.
mishnah-berurah/2:ו: (יב) Each for itself — permitted foot in its place does not forbid outside its place.
mishnah-berurah/2:ז: (יג) Permitted in its courtyard — inner does not forbid outer residents even though it has foot-traffic on it.
mishnah-berurah/3:א: (יד) Both forbidden — if the forgetful one is from the inner, certainly forbids the outer since it forbids in its place; even if forgetful from outer, outer is certainly forbidden and inner forbidden too though outer has no foot-traffic on it — since they joined together it is as dwelling in outer and forbids it; not helping that outer residents withdraw and close — eruv is not in their possession; main eruv is because dwelling as if dwelling where eruv is placed.
mishnah-berurah/3:ב: (טו) Until he nullifies his domain — to both courtyards as siman 381.
mishnah-berurah/3:ג: (טז) Both forbidden — considered one; unless he nullifies to both; but if nullifies only to inner residents it does not help even if they wish to withdraw from outer and close [later authorities].
mishnah-berurah/3:ד: (יז) Inner permitted — can withdraw from outer — "for my benefit you opened, not to harm" — uses for itself since eruv is with it; though initially partnered together, can retract and say not intending one of your courtyard would ruin and not give eruv share.
mishnah-berurah/4:א: (יח) Or two in outer and joined — those two alone, not with inner; teaches we do not decree lest they think two in inner like outer and permit here too — there certainly forbidden per forbidden foot in its place.
mishnah-berurah/4:ב: (יט) Individual in inner does not forbid, etc. — even without joining together, permitted foot in its place does not forbid outside its place.
mishnah-berurah/4:ג: (כ) Many like one individual — father with sons receiving sustenance from him, etc. — see siman 370.
peri-megadim/1:_: (א) Joined — in siman 372. Mechaber wrote open to reshus ha-rabbim — likewise to alley (Tur, Beit Yosef, Bach, Avkat Rochel). Three courtyards — only one outer wall open to reshus ha-rabbim or alley and middle foot-traffic with second outer — same law. Mechaber: eruv in middle in two houses — implies even if impossible in one house; one house as one vessel rule (Tosafos Yeshanim).
peri-megadim/2:_: (ב) And inner — if inner has way over outer and opening to reshus ha-rabbim and alley — can compel on Shabbat to withdraw from outer in such a case — Eruvin 86 seif 9 — see there.
peri-megadim/3:_: (ג) Both — wherever there is foot-traffic it forbids. Mechaber seif 2 each for itself permitted alone — permitted foot in its place does not forbid outside (Tosafos Yeshanim).
peri-megadim/4:_: (ד) Inner — if eruv in outer both forbidden — cannot one withdraw — eruv in outer and outer residents. Permitted foot does not forbid outside — see siman 364:3 Magen Avraham — specifically courtyard not alley; siman 392 seif 6; siman 372 Magen Avraham letter 2.
rabbi-akiva-eiger/1:_: See Mishna Berurah on nullifying domain when eruv in outer.
shaarei-teshuvah/1:_: See Avnei Nezer on eruv in two houses.
turei-zahav/1:_: Its eruv in this and that — then middle is like dwelling in them and outer residents do not dwell in middle — not like each other; if eruv in middle, all dwell in that house and courtyard.
turei-zahav/2:א: (ב) And inner open to outer — not to alley; thus inner has foot-traffic on outer since no entry from alley to inner except via outer.
turei-zahav/2:ב: (ב) Both forbidden — we hold forbidden foot in its place forbids outside its place.
turei-zahav/3:_: (ג) Inner permitted — can withdraw from outer — "for my benefit you opened, not to harm" — eruv is with it; though outer eruv placed in inner, said: for my benefit you dwelled, not to harm.
